name: Peptide Fragment Ion Predictor
tagline: Predict a/b/c/x/y/z fragment ions for linear and cyclic peptides, on a full structure diagram linked to a spectrum and table.
description: Enter a linear or head-to-tail cyclic peptide (ProForma-style modifications, D- and N-methyl residues, non-standard building blocks) and get every theoretical fragment ion for HCD, CID, ETD, EThcD or UVPD. Fragments are drawn on the full chemical structure, linked to a representative spectrum and a fragment table, and can be matched against a pasted peak list. Runs entirely in your browser.

inputs.name: sequence
inputs.label: Peptide sequence
inputs.help: One-letter codes (lowercase = D-residue), mods in brackets: PEPM[Oxidation]K, S[+79.9663], [Acetyl]-PEPTIDE-[Amidated]. Non-standard residues in parentheses or brackets: (Orn), [MeL], (D-Phe). cyclo(...) makes it cyclic.

inputs.name: topology
inputs.label: Topology
inputs.help: Linear peptides have N- and C-termini (a/b/c and x/y/z series). Head-to-tail cyclic peptides fragment by ring opening plus a second cleavage, giving contiguous b/a-type arcs (and c/z-type arcs in ETD).

inputs.name: precursorCharge
inputs.label: Precursor charge
inputs.help: Charge state of the isolated precursor. Fragment charges are capped at this value. ETD and EThcD need at least 2+.

inputs.name: activation
inputs.label: Fragmentation
inputs.help: Sets the default ion series and the intensity pattern of the representative spectrum: HCD/CID give b/y (b/a for rings), ETD gives c/z•, EThcD gives both, UVPD gives all six series.

inputs.name: ionTypes
inputs.label: Ion types
inputs.help: Which fragment series to compute. Leave on the preset to follow the chosen fragmentation method, or pick series individually (e.g. add c and z• to an HCD prediction).

inputs.name: maxFragmentCharge
inputs.label: Max fragment charge
inputs.help: Highest charge state computed for fragment ions (never above the precursor charge). 1–2 covers most HCD spectra of small peptides; use 3+ for long or very basic peptides.

inputs.name: losses
inputs.label: Neutral losses (H₂O, NH₃)
inputs.help: Adds −H₂O for fragments containing S, T, E or D and −NH₃ for fragments containing R, K, Q or N (residue-gated, as in ProteinProspector).

inputs.name: fixedMods
inputs.label: Fixed modifications
inputs.help: Applied to every matching residue, as Name@Site, comma separated: Carbamidomethyl@C, Oxidation@M, TMT6plex@K+N-term. Leave empty for none.

inputs.name: observed
inputs.label: Observed peaks (optional)
inputs.help: Paste a peak list to compare: one 'm/z intensity' pair per line (space, tab or comma), or an MGF spectrum. Matched peaks are annotated and drawn above the prediction (mirror plot).

inputs.name: tolerance
inputs.label: Match tolerance
inputs.help: Fragment mass tolerance for matching observed peaks. 10 ppm suits Orbitrap and Astral data; use about 0.4 Da (switch the unit) for ion-trap spectra.

inputs.name: toleranceUnit
inputs.label: Tolerance unit
inputs.help: ppm scales with m/z (high resolution); Da is a fixed window (low resolution, ion trap).

inputs.name: maxLosses
inputs.label: Max losses per fragment
inputs.help: How many neutral losses may combine on one fragment (2 allows b−2H₂O and b−H₂O−NH₃, which are common in cyclic peptides).

inputs.name: modLosses
inputs.label: Modification losses
inputs.help: Characteristic losses from modified residues: −H₃PO₄ from phospho, −CH₄SO from oxidised Met, −SO₃ from sulfation, −HexNAc from glycans.

inputs.name: adducts
inputs.label: Adduct ions
inputs.help: Also compute fragments carrying a metal or ammonium ion instead of one proton ([b+Na]⁺ etc.). Useful for sodiated precursors and some cyclic natural products.

inputs.name: immonium
inputs.label: Immonium ions
inputs.help: Low-mass immonium ions (residue − CO + H⁺), diagnostic for H, F, Y, W, L/I, P and modified residues.

inputs.name: precursorIons
inputs.label: Precursor ions
inputs.help: Adds [M+zH] for every charge plus precursor neutral losses, so unfragmented precursor peaks are labelled.

inputs.name: internal
inputs.label: Internal fragments (linear)
inputs.help: b-type and a-type internal fragments from two backbone cleavages (linear peptides only; every cyclic fragment is already internal).

inputs.name: internalMaxLength
inputs.label: Max internal length
inputs.help: Longest internal fragment (in residues) to compute. Short internal ions (2–4 residues) are the ones usually observed.

inputs.name: cyclicHydrolysis
inputs.label: b+H₂O ions (cyclic)
inputs.help: Cyclic only: arcs that carry an extra water (ring opened by hydrolysis), typical for depsipeptides and seen in some lactam rings.

outputs.name: ions
outputs.label: Fragment ion table
outputs.help: Every theoretical ion with label, sequence, charge, m/z and formula; observed m/z and ppm when a peak list is given.

examples.label: Angiotensin II, HCD 2+ (linear)
examples.description: Classic standard; values cross-checked against ProteinProspector MS-Product.

examples.label: Cyclosporin A, HCD 1+ (cyclic, N-methylated)
examples.description: 11 residues with MeBmt, Abu, Sar, MeLeu, D-Ala and MeVal; C62H111N11O12.

examples.label: Phosphopeptide, ETD 3+ (c/z•)
examples.description: ProForma modifications and ETD ion series.

alsoCite.text: Roepstorff P, Fohlman J. Proposal for a common nomenclature for sequence ions in mass spectra of peptides. Biomed Mass Spectrom 11, 601 (1984).
Ngoka LCM, Gross ML. A nomenclature system for labeling cyclic peptide fragments. J Am Soc Mass Spectrom 10, 360–363 (1999).

seo.title: Peptide Fragment Ion Calculator: linear & cyclic, b/y, c/z
seo.metaDescription: Free peptide fragment ion calculator for linear and cyclic peptides: a/b/c/x/y/z ions on a structure diagram, linked spectrum and table. Runs in your browser.

faq.q: How are b and y ion masses calculated?
faq.a: A singly protonated b ion is the sum of the N-terminal residue masses plus a proton (1.007276); a y ion is the sum of the C-terminal residue masses plus water (18.010565) plus a proton. For charge z, add z protons and divide by z.

faq.q: Why are there no y ions for a cyclic peptide?
faq.a: A head-to-tail ring has no termini. Fragmentation first opens the ring at one amide bond, giving a linear b-type ion with the precursor mass; a second cleavage releases contiguous b-type arcs. Ions that look like y ions are b ions from a different ring-opening site.

faq.q: What is the difference between z and z• ions?
faq.a: ETD produces radical z• ions (z+1, y − 16.019 Da). The even-electron z ion is y − NH3 (17.027 Da) and z+2 (z′) carries one more hydrogen. The tool lists the formula offset of each ion so naming conventions cannot be confused.

faq.q: Is the predicted spectrum a machine-learning prediction?
faq.a: No. Intensities come from a transparent rule set (ion-type weights per activation, proline and aspartic-acid effects, charge plausibility) plus each ion's isotope pattern. It shows which ions to expect, not exact intensities.
